procedure: Arrange the provided substances in separate, labelled containers.
Place a drop of each liquid or aqueous solution on separate red and blue litmus paper strips.
Observe and record any colour change in each strip for every substance.
Use the colour changes to decide whether each substance is acidic or basic in aqueous solution.
aim: To identify whether the given substances are acidic or basic using red and blue litmus paper.

viva.question: What colour does blue litmus turn in an acidic solution?
What colour does red litmus turn in a basic solution?
What happens to red and blue litmus in a neutral solution?
Why should separate strips be used for different substances?
viva.answer: To prevent one sample from contaminating another.

viva.question: Name one use of mineral acids.
viva.answer: Sulfuric acid is used in lead-acid batteries.

diagram: Draw two litmus strips beside a labelled sample drop; label the red litmus strip, blue litmus strip, sample, and observed colour change.
title: Testing substances with litmus paper
precautions: Use clean, separate droppers for different substances.
Use fresh, separate red and blue litmus strips for each sample.
Do not touch the litmus paper with wet or contaminated fingers.
Avoid contact with battery water and bleach; wash any splashes off skin immediately.
Record the colour change promptly and do not mix the samples.
result: Tap water was neutral; battery water and rain water were acidic. Soap solution, toothpaste, and bleach were basic, while the shampoo sample was acidic.
